subject: Hosted API capacity top-up and rateband clarification
messages:
From: Lisa Thompson <lisa@acmeretail.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmeretail.com
Date: 2025-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API capacity and rateband question

Hi Naomi,

Hope you’re well — growth has outpaced our forecast this quarter and we’re approaching our current monthly commit limits much faster than expected. Attached is our Q3 token usage report showing a 3.6x month-over-month increase on peak days.

We’re evaluating two things:
- A permanent increase to our hosted API monthly commit (we currently sit at 1.2B tokens/month)
- A short-term burst/bridge for the next 90 days to handle Black Friday traffic spikes without hitting soft-throttle windows.

Can you share: current ratebands at higher commit levels, any available intro or upsell discounts, and how burst pockets are typically provisioned (billing timing / invoice cadence)? We need a quick sizing + cost estimate to take to procurement.

Thanks — attaching Acme_Usage_Report_Q3.csv.

—Lisa
Lisa Thompson
Head of Platform Integrations
Acme Retail
From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Thompson <lisa@acmeretail.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2025-09-14T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity and rateband question

Hi Lisa — thanks for the report, this is exactly the kind of growth pattern we built our top-up paths for. Quick summary up front:

Option A — 2.5B/month committed (recommended)- New effective unit rate: 14% lower vs your current band- Includes 30% burst pocket for 90 days, billed monthly pro-rata- Latency and SLO unchanged, no change to network setup

Option B — 1.8B/month committed + larger burst pocket (temporary)- Smaller permanent uplift, bigger short-term cushion- Slightly higher unit rate than A but lower near-term OPEX

Operational notes:
- Burst pockets are added as a separate bucket on the invoice (consumed if commit is exceeded). We can structure them as a 90-day temporary pocket that either expires or converts to commit on Day 91.
- We can offer a 10% upsell credit for a 12-month renewal when you move to Option A.
- If you require invoicing to align with quarter boundaries, we can time the invoice for a prorated first month and then regular monthly billing thereafter.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm which option (A/B) you prefer — I can send a draft SOW and pricing sheet.
2) If you want discount consideration beyond the standard 10%, loop in your finance lead and I’ll bring in our sales manager (Karthik) to review.

I’m attaching a short sketch of the pricing bands and a copy of the usage file you sent so everyone stays on the same page.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, Lisa Thompson <lisa@acmeretail.com>, procurement@acmeretail.com
Date: 2025-09-14T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity and rateband question

Naomi / Lisa — looping in finance ops and legal considerations briefly. Pricing detail for internal reference (summary):

- Current band (1.2B): $0.00145/token effective
- Option B (1.8B): $0.00130/token effective (est.)
- Option A (2.5B): $0.00120/token effective + 10% upsell credit with 12-month commit

Burst pocket mechanics:
- Temporary burst bucket (90 days) priced at committed unit rate + 20% premium, billed monthly pro-rata
- If converted to commit in month 4, credit applied for consumed burst at the committed rate (so you only pay the premium for the temporary oversubscription period)

Docs and approvals:
- I’ll prepare a 1-page SOW + pricing annex; Naomi can send to Lisa for internal review.
- If procurement needs an earlier invoice date to align with PO timing, we can set the service start date to the first of next month and prorate the initial invoice.

DocuSign & approvals: please use this link to speed signature: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/signed-sow-acme-2025

Marissa — any compliance checklist items we should preemptively include for Acme?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, EMEA & NA | Redwood Inference
